newsitem.title: NIGERIA: At least one killed in Nigeria bomb blast.
newsitem.headline: At least one killed in Nigeria bomb blast.

text.p: A bomb exploded on a Nigerian army bus in Lagos on Tuesday, killing at least one person and wounding at least 15, military sources said.
It was the third blast in Lagos since December and followed a warning by the United States that bomb attacks might take place at Nigerian airports in the last two weeks of December.
No one has claimed responsibility but the authorities blame the explosions in politically volatile Nigeria on the exiled opposition.
Witnesses said the death toll in Tuesday's blast could be as high as four but there was no immediate confirmation of this.
They said the bomb went off in a bus carrying soldiers inside an army camp in the Surulere district of Lagos and the area had been cordoned off by security authorities.
"Investigations have commenced in the bomb blast this morning around Albati barracks," said one army source, who asked not to be identified.
"A bus full of soldiers was hit in very similar fashion to the last time," said a motor mechanic near the scene.
Last month a bomb planted in a rubbish dump ripped apart a bus carrying 60 soldiers, wounding 16 critically.

Two days earlier the military administrator of Lagos state, Colonel Muhammed Marwa, a close aide of military ruler General Sani Abacha, survived a bomb attack in which three people were seriously wounded.
